newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb destroys home on island of Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Bomb destroys home on island of Corsica.

text.p: A bomb planted by suspected Corsican separatists destroyed a home in the town of Cargese in the south of the Mediterranean island, but caused no injuries, police said on Wednesday.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast on Tuesday night. The owners of the building were away on holiday at the time.
Such bombings are virtually an everyday occurence on the resort island where separatist guerrillas have for two decades pursued greater autonomy from mainland France.
Economic difficulties have also brought conflict to the island.
Police clashed with angry farmers in the port of Bastia overnight in an unsuccessful effort to free the Danielle Casanova, a state-owned car ferry operating between Corsica and the mainland.
About a hundred farmers boarded the boat early on Tuesday and have prevented it leaving port in protest at economic difficulties in Corsica.
The protesters told reporters on Wednesday morning that they would maintain their occupation of the Danielle Casanova until the government sent an emissary from Paris to negotiate with them.
A second boat, the Paglia Orba, was sent to the island from the mainland to maintain ferry service.
